description: Agenet is a Python package developed to estimate Age of Information in cooperative wireless communication networks. It represents a source, a decode-and-forward relay and a destination, using finite-blocklength communication assumptions over Rayleigh fading channels. Users vary transmission power, power allocation, packet size and block length. The package calculates signal-to-noise ratio, block error rate and theoretical or simulated information age, with a command-line program for parameter experiments. Network dimensions and update times are configured by the user, so there is no fixed geographical coverage or historical observation period. Public repositories, documentation and a PyPI distribution provide the software free under MIT. These calculations support the design of time-sensitive communication links and comparisons between freshness and reliability assumptions. A limitation is that the represented three-node relay system and channel model simplify a deployed communications network. No directly related existing catalogue record was established. This review inspected the code documentation and metadata without running simulations or validating device performance.
